record.paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
record.context_brief: Effective degrees of freedom in high-density QCD
record.original_question: Are classical fields still the correct effective degrees of freedom for describing the many-body system of strongly correlated gluons in QCD at high parton density, especially in the parton-saturation regime explored by proton-nucleus and electron-nucleus collisions?

evidence.quote: The Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory has emerged as the best candidate to approximate QCD in the saturation regime, both in terms of practical applicability and of phenomenological success [1].

There are more fundamental questions, still unexplored, in the field of QCD at high parton density. How does the transition from the saturation regime to confinement happen? Does the QCD coupling run with Qs? Are classical fields still the right degrees of freedom? What are the universality properties of the saturation regime? p+A and e+A collisions offer special opportunities to explore this many-body system of strongly-correlated gluons.

artifact.category_tag: Color Glass Condensate and parton saturation
artifact.self_contained_problem:
In quantum chromodynamics (QCD) at very high parton density, the gluon occupation numbers in the wavefunction of a hadron or nucleus become parametrically large at transverse momenta below a dynamically generated saturation scale Q_s. In this regime it has been proposed that the strongly correlated many-body system of gluons admits an effective description in terms of classical color gauge fields A^μ_a sourced by static color charges ρ_a with a stochastic weight functional W[ρ] (the Color Glass Condensate framework), so that observables are computed by solving the classical Yang–Mills equations D_μ F^{μν}_a = J^ν_a together with a renormalization group evolution of W[ρ] in rapidity (the JIMWLK / B-K hierarchy).

Determine whether classical color gauge fields remain the correct effective degrees of freedom for describing this many-body system of strongly correlated gluons in the parton-saturation regime probed by proton–nucleus and electron–nucleus collisions. Specifically:

(a) Identify, from first principles in QCD, the precise window in (x, Q^2, A) where a classical-field description is parametrically justified, and quantify the leading corrections (quantum, NLO, and beyond-eikonal) that break the classicality assumption.

(b) Establish whether observables in p+A and e+A collisions in the saturation regime are universal functions of Q_s alone, or whether additional non-classical degrees of freedom (e.g. odderon-like correlators, fluctuations of Q_s, fully quantum Wilson-line operators) are required for a consistent effective theory.

(c) Characterize the transition between the saturation/classical regime and the confinement regime, and decide whether classical fields can describe this transition or whether a different set of effective degrees of freedom must take over.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether classical color fields are the correct effective degrees of freedom in saturated QCD remains open. The Color Glass Condensate framework continues to be developed (NLO JIMWLK/B-K, sub-eikonal corrections, small-x evolution) and is being tested at the LHC and the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider, but no first-principles QCD derivation establishes its validity beyond the leading classical regime, and competing or complementary descriptions (resummed perturbative QCD, holographic methods) are still actively investigated.

status_evidence.title: The Color Glass Condensate (review)
status_evidence.snippet: The CGC is an effective theory for the small-x degrees of freedom in QCD; classical fields and their quantum evolution form the basis, but a complete proof of their adequacy in all of the saturation regime is lacking.
status_evidence.claim: Classical-field/CGC description is the leading approximation; corrections and validity beyond leading order are still under active study.

status_evidence.title: Electron-Ion Collider Yellow Report
status_evidence.snippet: e+A collisions at the EIC are designed to probe the saturation regime and test the CGC effective theory, indicating the underlying questions remain open and experimentally driven.
status_evidence.claim: The community treats the validity of classical-field effective degrees of freedom in saturated QCD as an open question to be tested experimentally.
